mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above the prior 12-month average precedes a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to tightened discount rates affecting future equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in >70% of post-trigger windows, or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 12-month average for ≥30 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (employment) coincides with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market strength supports corporate optimism and higher earnings expectations.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.05 over 60-day windows during expansion, or 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in HOUST (residential construction) followed by a rise above the 12-month low predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals improving housing demand and economic momentum.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day returns after such HOUST reversals in >50% of cases, or the 12-month low is not clearly identified.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO (industrial production) below the prior 6 months' average, sustained for two consecutive months, predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it indicates supply-side weakness and potential deflationary pressure.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in >60% of such contraction episodes, or INDPRO recovers rapidly without lagged negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls by more than 0.2 percentage points in a single month, the S&P 500 shows a positive 5-day forward return as lower labor costs ease inflationary pressures.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in >50% of such UNRATE declines, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in RSAFS (retail sales) for three consecutive months indicates strengthening consumer demand, which is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.1 over 60-day windows during acceleration, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both GDPC1 (GDP) and CPIAUCSL (CPI) for two consecutive months suggest demand softening, which precedes a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative in >50% of such episodes, or the co-movement is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS below 3.5%), a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return is expected as lower policy rates encourage equity valuation expansion.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in >70% of easing episodes, or FEDFUNDS rises above 3.5% before 60 days.
